task_name: Sterling Row - Residence launch film and viewing package
client_brief:
Sterling Row is nine full floor residences in a converted warehouse block, and we are opening the release on the broker's channel. The footage is honest about its limits: every supplied clip runs five seconds and carries no audio, so this is a short form package, not a long film. Build a restrained launch film and a vertical teaser for the channel, both carried by quiet on screen text rather than a voice. The brick and oak of the interiors keep their natural warmth under one near-neutral, slightly cool grade, without drifting into a different colour world from shot to shot, and the building and residence details must stay truthful.

What we need back
- Residence launch film: 1 named export, 12 to 15 seconds, 16:9, under the supplied instrumental bed. It opens on the approved tagline, carries one residence fact card taken from the specification sheet that gives the residence's name, floor, square footage and exposure, and closes on the viewing action with the Sterling Row wordmark set small on that closing card.
- Residence vertical teaser: 1 named export, 6 to 8 seconds, 9:16, cut from the same material. The development identity is clear through the Sterling Row wordmark, set small and shown before the closing card, and the teaser ends on the viewing action.
- The still and print items are not part of this package: deliver only the two films above.

House rules for this package
- The approved viewing action is set exactly as: Viewings by appointment. It is the last thing on screen on both films.
- No narration. The broker's recorded read (sterlingrow_broker_read.wav) stays out of this cut; we would rather say less than lay a voice over five second clips. Both films run under the supplied bed, sterlingrow_bed.wav.
- On screen copy stays small and minimal, in the approved language only. Never say luxury lifestyle, act now, limited time or dream home, and never burn a price into a frame.
- Video delivery means a playable MP4, not a storyboard, still montage PDF or editing log. Live action edits require adequate distinct footage: looping one short clip is not a substitute for the missing coverage.

Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Permission restrictions in the owner's notes take precedence over inclusion in a source table. Use the attached brand identity and the source files listed in the asset manifest. The output register defines exact filenames, pages, sizes and record bindings. Supporting previews are welcome but cannot replace those files.

brand_identity.sector: Luxury residential: full floor residences in a converted warehouse block, sold through a single broker's video channel.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022, a converted warehouse block of nine full floor residences, sold one at a time through one broker's channel of three or four videos a month.
brand_identity.about: Sterling Row is nine full floor residences in a converted warehouse block, starting just over four million dollars, sold to buyers who are not in a hurry and have seen everything. The channel is where most buyers first meet the broker, so every piece has to feel made by one hand. Restraint is the whole proposition: these buyers are reassured, not persuaded.
brand_identity.audience: Ultra high net worth buyers, typically on their third or fourth property, reassured by evidence and calm rather than by benefit claims, who still need the floor, the square footage and the exposure before they ask to view.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Full floor residences from just over four million dollars, the top of the market. Presentation sits near neutral and deliberately small: anything that looks like a promotion reads, at this tier, as a building that is struggling to sell.

brand_identity.typography: Sterling Row sets words in Geist Regular and numbers in Geist Mono, and never mixes the two. The opening card sets Geist Regular at 42 px on 48 px leading, tracked minus 0.010 em, and 11 pt in print. Every floor, square footage, price and date sets in Geist Mono at 26 px on 32 px, tabular, tracking zero, in Cast Brass on Near Black and ranged on one right edge. Labels and standing text set Geist Regular at 20 px on 30 px, tracked plus 0.060 em, no more than 65 characters a line, and the fixed disclosure sets Geist Regular at 16 px on 22 px, tracked plus 0.020 em. No numeral is ever set in the text face, wherever it falls.
brand_identity.voice: Spare, composed, confident without pressure. Example: "Nine residences. Full floor. Sold one at a time, to buyers in no hurry."

brand_identity.values: Discretion and accuracy. The developer's restraint rules and disclosure lines are contractual, and the brand is protected by never looking like it is selling.

rules: Never set a numeral in the text face; every floor, square footage, price and date sets in Geist Mono.
Figures set tabular in Cast Brass on Near Black and range on one right edge, one alignment for the whole piece.
A numeral inside a sentence still breaks out into Geist Mono; if that reads badly, the number is written as a word instead.
The disclosure wording is fixed by the developer and cannot be changed.
The developer's restraint rules are contractual: nothing may look like a promotion, since at this tier that reads as a building struggling to sell.
In print the opening card sets 11 pt and the rest of the scale holds the same proportion.

palette_rules.distribution: On screen, Near Black is the only ground for type: every text card, and every panel that carries type, is solid Near Black, and no type is set directly on footage (type_system steps 02 and 03 set every figure and word on Near Black). Every figure, with the step 02 figure line it sits in, is Cast Brass in Geist Mono; every other word is Warm White or Stone Grey, either one or both. Cast Brass is otherwise used only for hairline rules, as on sterlingrow_spec_sheet.pdf, and those rules cover no more than 5% of the designed, non-footage area of any card; Cast Brass figures are type and are not counted. Slate is optional with no required on-screen use: it never colours a word or figure, and it may fill a solid panel that carries no type, as it fills the panel behind the photograph on sterlingrow_spec_sheet.pdf. The recovered wordmark is judged by the wordmark checks, not by these type colour, effect or palette rules.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, glow, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour or type, and no scrim, vignette, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over footage. A panel is a solid, fully opaque area of a palette colour, Near Black wherever it carries type, laid over part of a shot that otherwise fills the frame, such as a lower third: it is not an overlay, whereas any translucent, gradient or feathered area over footage is. Footage shrunk inside Near Black bands, with or without type in them, is a letterbox or pillarbox, not a panel. A card or line may cut or fade in and out as a whole; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, cards, panels or rules. Apart from the recovered wordmark, no metallic, foil, glow, shadow or gradient effect on any type, Cast Brass figures included, which stay flat #B08D57. Nothing that looks like a promotion, which the type rules forbid: no price on screen and no large benefit caption in any colour.
palette_rules.photography: Footage keeps its own colour: the brick and oak keep their natural warmth under one grade that sits near neutral and slightly cool, as sterlingrow_brand_note.txt sets (clean whites, no crushed blacks, no warm saturated push). White walls, cabinets and window light read the same near-neutral white in every shot, so no shot drifts into a different colour world; the natural colour of brick, oak and sky is not a grade shift. No palette colour is laid over footage as a tint, duotone or colour wash, and no pixels are generated or extended to reframe a clip; cropping to the delivery ratio is allowed.

truth_constraints: Do not invent names, prices, claims, product features, locations, credentials, records, or documentary events that are absent from the approved inputs.
Do not silently replace a weak supplied asset. Use it honestly, reject it with a reason, or take only the brief's declared Stock or concept exception.
Record every omission, substitution, reconciliation, and material quality compromise in the delivery manifest.
Treat measured file duration and stream metadata as authoritative. Do not infer spoken content from silent clips or use a visual summary as a transcript.
production_requirements: Use the supplied approved copy and factual records. Do not invent claims, prices, dates, credentials or product features.
A clean preview is not a final file. Supply every named export.
Retouching, masks, crop matrices and contact sheets support production; they do not replace the commissioned finished collateral.
